# PB-02 optimization proposals

These are proposed follow-up scopes, not changes implemented by PB-02. Keep the
provisional 1 ms transition / 25 ms event admission / 100 ms ready dispatch
budgets. Do not widen namespace limits or collect unresolved work to pass them.
The measured source is `911fc5dc7d509688a078ff1715eda715b0b81cf1` plus the
inventoried benchmark harness; it is not PB-01's `921208a` source bundle.

## PB-03: Remove repeated immutable-artifact work from unchanged CAS commits

The PostgreSQL `Storage::compare_and_swap` path in
`crates/aq-playbooks-postgres/src/lib.rs` loads the previous snapshot and all
artifact bytes, locks the union of artifact addresses, then verifies,
canonicalizes, inserts/selects and compares every installed artifact on every
namespace mutation. Fixed costs remain even for a no-consumer event and a small
namespace. The five-artifact experiment already misses the 25 ms event budget at
zero retained history, while pure closure evaluation and MemoryStorage are much
smaller. This suggests a focused first experiment; it does not by itself assign
all fixed latency to one SQL loop.

Instrument round trips, canonical artifact validation and snapshot/index work
separately, then avoid redundant work for proven unchanged immutable addresses.
Use ownership/incarnation/revision and installed-address evidence; do not trust
an arbitrary caller's replacement object or a display name. Keep cold-cache and
arbitrary `Storage` caller validation paths explicit. Do not weaken artifact
reference/disposal locking to remove a round trip.

Acceptance must preserve immutable-address conflicts, integrity validation,
artifact-GC races and namespace retention references, ownership/CAS conflicts,
transaction rollback, protection authenticated contexts/key rotation and cold
restart behavior. Repeat PB-02's exact five-artifact and reduced profiles with
fsync enabled, including root/event/receipt growth, before claiming improvement.
No schema/protocol changes should be hidden in a cache-only optimization.

## PB-04: Bound transition persistence cost as settled history grows

`Engine::transaction` in `crates/aq-playbooks-runner/src/lib.rs` loads a whole
namespace, evaluates a closure, synchronizes indexes, serializes the complete
state for quota admission, and commits it. PostgreSQL CAS again decodes the prior
snapshot and writes a whole JSONB snapshot alongside index/projection changes.
The 512-root/event profile is approximately 1.25 MB canonical state, far below the
64 MiB admission limit, yet event p95 is already well above 25 ms. MemoryStorage
also grows markedly, so SQL round trips alone cannot solve the history slope.

Design a versioned incremental transition/dirty-record persistence path or an
equally bounded alternative. Measure allocation, serialization and SQL work to
choose the smallest implementation that changes this slope. Preserve the public
atomic boundary for events, receipts, waits, owned children, effect intents,
indexes and quota checks. An index query must not become an alternate task-state
owner or a source of unbounded scans. Keep a defined migration/fallback path for
existing snapshots and protection providers; do not bypass integrity or quota
checks merely because they currently scan the snapshot.

Acceptance must prove crash/rollback and restart equivalence to the reference
snapshot implementation, revision/incarnation fencing, deterministic IDs and
replay, fair ready/effect discovery, producer responsibility on refusal,
protection/rotation behavior and quota refusal without unresolved-work eviction.
Repeat all PB-02 sizes and explicitly declare synchronous load/commit and memory
costs. Concurrent admission is a separate admission-policy concern: four
producers exhausting bounded CAS retries is an explicit refusal, not permission
to drop their work or silently retry without a bound. AQ-12 must place synchronous
storage away from async control handlers and declare a bounded ingress policy.

Both follow-ups should block broader performance qualification. Neither this
experiment nor these proposals establish a 500-agent product profile; PERF-01
must test the assembled product under its declared workload.
